original_question: Improve the current upper bound 6k + 6 on the chromatic number of a bar k-visibility graph.
target_in_paper: Open Problem 23 in §3.3, “Bar Visibility Graphs”: improve the current upper bound 6k+6 on the chromatic number of a bar k-visibility graph. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s exact target very closely: it identifies the right graph class (bar k-visibility graphs), the right invariant (chromatic number), and the exact bound 6k+6 that the paper names immediately before stating Open Problem 23. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
missing_details: The parameter should be quantified explicitly: k is a nonnegative integer, and the problem asks for a bound that works uniformly for every such k. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

To make the question stand alone, you should define a bar k-visibility graph: vertices are represented by pairwise disjoint horizontal bars in the plane, and two vertices are adjacent exactly when there exists a vertical segment joining their bars that intersects at most k other bars. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

The question is about a universal upper bound on χ(G) for every finite bar k-visibility graph G, not about improving the bound for a special subclass or a single example. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
The notation χ(G) for the chromatic number should be introduced if the question is to be mathematically self-contained. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
If one wants maximal paper-faithfulness, one can note that the bar k-visibility notion is the strong vertical-visibility version discussed in §3.3. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree restriction, nilpotency condition, or 'for all sufficiently large m' clause is relevant here; the omitted details are purely graph-theoretic and representational. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
refined_question: For each integer k≥0, improve the current general upper bound χ(G)≤6k+6 for bar k-visibility graphs: determine a smaller universal function f(k) such that every finite graph G that admits a representation by pairwise disjoint horizontal bars in the plane, with uv∈E(G) if and only if some vertical segment joining the bars for u and v intersects at most k other bars, satisfies χ(G)≤f(k). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
justification: The draft is not aiming at the paper’s introduction-level conjectures on point visibility graphs; it is aimed at §3.3 on bar visibility graphs. In that section, the paper defines bar k-visibility graphs, records that Dean et al. proved χ(G)≤6k+6, and then states Open Problem 23 exactly as improving that upper bound. The refined version therefore keeps the scope exactly there, adding only the missing quantifiers and the definition needed to make the problem stand alone, without drifting into neighboring open problems on characterization, forbidden subgraphs, regularity, thickness, or crossing number. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
